title: Unboxing Videos for Product Launches | AIVideosUGC
description: Plan unboxing videos for product launches: a teaser before, a full reveal on launch day, and a closer look after. Use a package photo and make your first clip.
h1: How to Use Unboxing Videos for Product Launches
lead: Unboxing videos for a launch work best as three short clips. A teaser shows the closed box before you start selling. Then comes a reveal on launch day, and a closer look once people ask what is in the box. Start from the package photo or a product link. Then add a presenter, a script, and a voice.
summary: Plan three short clips around launch day from one package photo. Add the date and the price yourself, and keep the reveal after launch week.

paras: What the clip should show, how that compares with filming, and the three steps. It also covers what you can change, how long each clip is, where the date and price go, and how shops use the set.

sections.h2: Show the Product, the Unboxing, and a Voiceover
paras: Put the product in a presenter's hands, so a shopper can judge the size, the shape, and the finish. You do not need a studio day.
Show the unboxing itself: a hand on the lid, the tissue, and the item coming out. Show the closed box first, open it on launch day, and follow with one closer detail.
Add a short spoken line that names what is inside. You can edit that line before it is set. This format fits earbuds, candles, skincare sets, and gift boxes.
sections.alt: Hands open a blank kraft parcel to reveal one plain cream ceramic travel mug wrapped in tissue.

sections.h2: Filming the Unboxing vs Starting From a Photo
paras: Cost. A filmed unboxing pays a person, a place, and an edit. A 6 second clip costs 24 credits, and a 10 second clip costs 40 credits. A 15 second clip costs 60 credits, and a 30 second clip costs 120 credits. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits. Pro is $35 for 300. Premium is $63 for 600.
Timing. You start when the package photo exists. You do not wait on a booked crew.
How many clips. One photo feeds the teaser, the reveal, and the closer look. Each of those is its own clip.
Who is there. One person on the shop team can make the three clips.
Another version. A new sentence makes another clip when you want a different opening. The credit cost shows before you start. If a clip fails to finish, those credits come back.

sections.h2: How to Make a Launch Unboxing in 3 Simple Steps
paras: Start from a photo of the box you will mail, or paste the link in [URL to video](page:url-to-video).
Pick an adult from the [actor library](page:ai-actors), and use that saved face on all three clips.
Shorten the draft script to one motion. Leave the date and the price out of that line.

sections.h2: What Photo Should a Product Launch Unboxing Video Start From?
paras: Use a clear photo of the product in the packaging people will receive. Shoot it in daylight, with any print facing the camera.

If the box design is still changing, wait until you can photograph the package people will receive. The clip follows that photo, and the box you describe. A stand-in box becomes the box shoppers expect. Count what ships. If the kit includes a cable, a pouch, and a card, those items should come out. A product link can fill the first draft. You still replace any photo that is not the package you will mail.

sections.h2: Which AI Unboxing Video Ideas Fit Launch Week?
paras: Plan a teaser, a reveal, and a closer look. Each one uses the same package photo and its own sentence. Use one saved presenter on all three.

The teaser shows the closed box and a hand on the lid. The reveal opens the tissue and lifts the product out. The closer look turns one detail, such as a lid, a clasp, or a cable. [AI product video generator](page:product-videos) fits when you want a demo after the open. [AI image to video](page:image-to-video) fits when a photo of the closed box should simply start to move.
sections.alt: Hands lift the lid of a blank kraft parcel to begin revealing one plain cream ceramic travel mug.

sections.h2: How Do I Write the Scene for Each Launch Clip?
paras: Name the box, the hands, and the one motion. Leave the date and the price out of that sentence. A drafted script can suggest the line. You shorten it to that one motion.

The teaser can be "Hands rest on the lid of a plain kraft box, in soft daylight." The reveal can be "Hands lift the lid and raise one cream mug out of the tissue." The closer look names the one detail you want turned toward the camera. Keep each sentence to one motion. Change the voice if the tone does not fit the shop. Read the captions before you post.

sections.h2: What You Can Set on the Launch Clip
paras: Start from a photo or a product link. You do not need another editor app to get the first clip.
Change the script, the voice, the video shape, and the colors before you download.
A voice reads the line at a natural pace. Swap it if it does not sound like your shop.
Use 9:16, a tall phone video, for TikTok, Reels, or Shorts. Use 1:1, a square, for a feed. Use 16:9, a wide video, for a product page or a normal YouTube video.
Pick a presenter from the actor library, the list of adult faces. Or save one face for the whole launch week.
Edit the draft script so the spoken line matches the one motion in the clip. You decide the final words. The same line can be spoken in another language for a second market.

sections.h2: How Long Should an Unboxing Video for New Products Be?
paras: Use 6 seconds for the teaser, and 10 seconds to open and show the product. Use 15 seconds for a slower reveal, and 30 seconds for a kit with several items.

In that same order, they cost 24, 40, 60, and 120 credits. The cost shows before each clip starts. If a clip fails, the credits come back. Each length is its own clip. Make the length you need for [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok). Make a longer one if the product page should show more of the unboxing.

sections.h2: How Do I Add the Date and Price to a Short Unboxing Clip?
paras: Captions can follow the spoken line. You still type the date, the price, and any code yourself, so they match the store.

Put the date, and a few words such as "Coming soon", on the teaser. Put "Available now" and the price on the reveal. Pick a song from the music library in the editor, or a track you already licensed for ads. The music library is the song list on this site. Trim the clip there. Then send the file to TikTok or Meta, or download it with no watermark. Post the teaser first. Switch to the reveal when the product page is live. Save the closer look for the next week. A catalog can also send the same work through the API. The API lets your shop's own system send the product and get the file back. Keep the teaser text short, so people can read it while the clip plays.

sections.h2: How Shops Use a Launch Unboxing
paras: A skincare shop shows a presenter lifting the bottle out of the tissue and naming the size that ships.
A gadget shop shows the cable, the pouch, and the card coming out in that order.
A candle shop uses the closed box as the teaser and the lid lift as the reveal.
A food shop keeps the voice on the flavor printed on the jar, not on a claim about results.
A jewelry shop uses the closer look to turn the clasp toward the camera.
A shop with two markets keeps the same unboxing and speaks the line in the other language.
A two-person team makes all three clips from one package photo.
A marketplace seller pastes the listing link, then replaces any photo that is not the package they will mail.
A shop that wants two opening lines writes a second sentence and keeps the same presenter.
A home shop posts the teaser, then swaps in the reveal on the morning the page goes live.
Use one real package photo, one saved presenter, and three sentences, for the teaser, the reveal, and the closer look. You add your own date and price.

Do not show a box or a part the buyer will not receive. Six seconds costs 24 credits, and ten seconds costs 40 credits. Fifteen seconds costs 60 credits, and thirty seconds costs 120 credits. After you check the unboxing, download it with no watermark, or send it to TikTok or Meta.

faq.q: How do I make an unboxing video for a launch?
faq.a: Photograph the package people will receive. Or paste the product link, and replace any photo that is not that package. Pick a presenter, shorten the script to one motion, and check the unboxing before you post.

faq.q: Can I start from a product link?
faq.a: Yes. The link can draft the script and pull photos from the page. The box in the finished clip still has to be the one you will mail.

faq.q: What if the video shows something that is not in my box?
faq.a: Do not post that version. Make it again and name the exact contents, such as a bottle, a pump, and a pouch. Shoppers will compare their package with the unboxing they saw.

faq.q: How long should an unboxing clip be?
faq.a: Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Six is a teaser. Ten opens and shows the product. Fifteen is a slower reveal. Thirty covers a kit with several items.

faq.q: What photo should I start from?
faq.a: Use a clear photo of the product or the package, and list every item in the box. Check the opening, the reveal, and the final contents against the real package.

faq.q: How many credits does an unboxing clip use?
faq.a: A 6 second clip uses 24 credits, and a 10 second clip uses 40 credits. A 15 second clip uses 60 credits, and a 30 second clip uses 120 credits. If the clip fails, the credits come back.

faq.q: What if my packaging is still changing?
faq.a: Wait until you can photograph the final package. Describe the box people will receive, not a stand-in.

faq.q: Can one package photo make several launch clips?
faq.a: Yes. Reuse the photo, keep one saved presenter, and write a separate sentence for the teaser, the reveal, and the closer look.

faq.q: Can I change the voice, the music, and the captions?
faq.a: Yes. Change the voice, pick a song from the music library or one you licensed, and read the captions. Type the date, the price, and any code yourself.

faq.q: Can I send the clip to TikTok or Meta?
faq.a: Yes. After you check the unboxing, send it to TikTok or Meta (Facebook and Instagram). Or download it with no watermark, meaning no logo on the file.

cta_lead: Turn one package photo into a teaser, a reveal, or a follow-up clip, then check it against the real box.
